data.title: AI TRENDS | Amber Group to Focus More on AI Investment and Incubation, Adjust Trading and Market-Making Operations
data.description: Amber Group said it is placing greater emphasis on AI-related investment and incubation while adjusting the scale and capital allocated to its market-making and trading businesses. According to Foresight News, the company sees significant long-term opportunities in AI and is shifting more of its business and resources to the sector. The changes will affect some team members, whom Amber Group said it will support through the transition. The company added that its businesses are continuing to operate.

data.title: AI TRENDS | South Korea's Financial Regulator Asks Financial Companies to Report AI Exposure
data.description:
According to Sina Finance, South Korea's Financial Supervisory Service has asked major domestic financial companies to disclose their exposure to the artificial intelligence industry. Choi Beom-jeon, head of the agency's financial industry supervision group, said the regulator is assessing exposure as a precaution amid growing concerns about hyperscale data centers and AI companies. The first-of-its-kind survey covers large firms, including banks, brokerages and insurers, and asks about direct or indirect investments in AI companies and direct lending relationships; some firms have already submitted questionnaires.

The assessment aims to gauge South Korean companies' vulnerabilities in the AI sector. South Korea is viewed as a bellwether for the regional AI boom, while global scrutiny of the technology is increasing. AI has attracted hundreds of billions of dollars in investment, most of it debt-financed.

data.title: Deutsche Bank Raises Dollar Forecasts, Citing Exceptional Market Conditions
data.description: According to CNBC, Deutsche Bank raised its U.S. dollar forecasts, citing an unusual market environment in which the artificial intelligence boom lifted U.S. real rates and drove large equity inflows. Strategists including Tim Baker and George Saravelos expect the dollar to strengthen in the first half of next year, weaken modestly in the second half and remain elevated overall. They expect the dollar to drift lower only later in 2027, while staying strong, and forecast the euro at $1.15 and the dollar at 145 yen at the end of 2027. The strategists also cited fiscal and current account deficits, potential trade tariffs and the possibility of President Donald Trump turning to foreign policy amid domestic policy obstacles as risks to the currency.

data.title: AI | Enrique Lores Calls AI Commerce an Opportunity for PayPal
data.description: PayPal President and CEO Enrique Lores called the shift toward AI-driven, agentic commerce an “incredible opportunity” for the company, saying trust, security and identity are becoming increasingly important, according to Bloomberg. He also discussed PayPal’s turnaround, expansion into financial services and investment in AI in an interview with Haslinda Amin on the sidelines of Singapore Fintech Festival 2026.

data.title: PRECIOUS METALS | Investors Increasingly Question Gold’s Safe-Haven Role
data.description:
According to Jin10, investors are increasingly questioning gold’s traditional role as a safe-haven asset in portfolios. In recent months, gold prices have fallen sharply even as risk assets such as stocks suffered steep sell-offs. George Cheveley, a portfolio manager at Ninety One, said gold had performed “more like a risk asset” than a hedge against risk.

Peel Hunt analysts said there was “no clear trigger” for gold’s fall to a new low this week; falling oil prices and bond yields should, in fact, have supported gold. They added that the price break below $3,800 per ounce looked like “potential capitulation selling” by investors. This raised concerns that market sentiment was deteriorating and that more investors saw a need to close positions and stay on the sidelines as the new year approached.

John Reade, the World Gold Council’s strategist for Asian and European markets, said this year’s weakness in gold was “largely due to leveraged Western speculators and investors”—short-term participants who entered as prices rose rapidly and exited quickly when economic conditions changed. Helen Amos, managing director and commodities analyst at the Bank of Montreal, said investors had warned that they no longer viewed gold as a diversification tool in stock portfolios.

data.title: Ripple CEO Says Crypto Selling Pressure May Reverse After Anthropic IPO
data.description:
Ripple CEO Brad Garlinghouse said some recent selling pressure in crypto markets stems from investors shifting funds to high-profile IPOs such as Anthropic.

According to Odaily, he expects capital flows to change after Anthropic completes its listing, potentially allowing crypto markets to rebound.

Garlinghouse compared the situation with market performance after SpaceX’s listing, saying pressure from funds being diverted to large IPOs may be temporary.

data.title: UK Treasury Opposes Key Plan to Address Youth Unemployment
data.description: According to Jin10, the Financial Times reported that the UK Treasury is opposing a key plan to address youth unemployment. Under the plan, businesses hiring young people in the UK would receive a reduction in their employer National Insurance contributions. The move has sparked dissatisfaction among the business community.

data.title: South Africa Seen Keeping Rates Steady, With Hike Possible in 2027
data.description:
South Africa’s central bank is expected to leave borrowing costs unchanged for now, with a hike possible in 2027, Bloomberg reported.

Oil prices have eased, and there are few signs that a recent energy-price surge is having a lasting effect on broader inflation.

data.title: Google's Porat Calls for Local Jobs Investment Near Data Centers Amid Backlash
data.description: Alphabet Inc. Chief Investment Officer Ruth Porat said the company and its peers need to invest in jobs in communities where data centers are being built, as projects across the country face backlash, according to Bloomberg.

data.title: AI | Anthropic Gray-Market Shares Point to Gains of 22% to 26%
data.description: According to Bloomberg, Anthropic PBC shares were indicated to open 22% to 26% higher in gray-market trading after the AI lab’s upsized $107.3 billion initial public offering and private placement broke SpaceX’s record.

data.title: Bitcoin Spot ETFs See $306 Million in Net Outflows; None of 12 Funds Records Inflows
data.description:
Bitcoin spot ETFs recorded $306 million in net outflows on November 18, with none of the 12 funds reporting an inflow.

According to Odaily, citing SoSoValue data, the largest single-day outflow was $149 million from IBIT, whose cumulative net inflows totaled $63.911 billion. FBTC saw $69.3108 million in outflows, while its cumulative net inflows reached $10.074 billion. As of publication, the funds had total net assets of $77.707 billion, a net-asset ratio of 6.17%, and cumulative net inflows of $54.095 billion.

data.title: Morgan Stanley Adds $32 Million in Bitcoin Exposure Through Strive Shares
data.description: According to ChainCatcher citing Crypto Briefing, Morgan Stanley increased its stake in Nasdaq-listed Bitcoin treasury company Strive (ASST) by 326,608 shares, bringing its total holdings to 1,749,530 shares. The purchase expanded its position by nearly a quarter and added an estimated $32 million in Bitcoin-related exposure.

data.title: Bitbase Plans Platform Token, Says Points Will Be Linked to It
data.description:
Bitbase plans to launch a platform token and link its points to the token, Chief Business Officer Nicholas Lo said in a live interview with Cointelegraph. According to Foresight News, the token’s name, launch date and redemption ratio have not been announced.

Bitbase points launched on November 4, with the first phase scheduled to last 26 weeks and distribute 1 million points each week. More than 17,000 users received points during the first week.

data.title: Hyperscale Data’s Michigan AI Project Needs $74.8 Million, Faces Going-Concern Doubts
data.description: Hyperscale Data says its Michigan AI data center project will require another $74.8 million from November 2026 through March 2027. According to Odaily, the company said in a regulatory filing that its current funds and available financing are insufficient to cover planned spending and obligations over the next 12 months, raising substantial doubt about its ability to continue as a going concern. At the end of September, the company had $17 million in unrestricted cash and $231 million in current liabilities. Since the end of July, it has sold about 1,113 BTC for proceeds of about $74 million. Construction and equipment costs for the project are estimated at $122.1 million, of which $47.3 million had been paid by October. An agreement with an AI customer has a potential value of up to $1.2 billion, contingent on two customer renewals and the company’s performance.

data.title: Walmart to Report Earnings Before the Bell; Analysts See 64 Cents per Share, $187.27 Billion in Revenue
data.description: According to CNBC, Walmart is scheduled to report its fiscal third-quarter results Thursday, with analysts surveyed by LSEG expecting earnings per share of 64 cents and revenue of $187.27 billion. The company previously forecast third-quarter net sales growth of 3% to 3.75%. UBS analysts said they expect healthy market-share gains and robust operating-income growth in the fiscal fourth quarter. Walmart shares have fluctuated this year but are up roughly 13% year-to-date.

data.title: UK Financial Cyber Incident Reports Hit Second-Highest Level in Five Years in October
data.description:
According to Sina Finance, the Financial Conduct Authority (FCA) said Thursday that it received 38 cybersecurity incident reports in October, the second-highest monthly total in five years. The only higher count was 49 reports in June 2023, during the MOVEit data breach. October's total was more than 50% above the previous peak recorded 18 months earlier.

The FCA and the Bank of England proposed new guidance to clarify expectations for banks, insurers and other financial institutions on preventing and detecting cyberattacks and recovering from them. The draft sets out more detailed expectations for cyber resilience, governance, incident response, recovery and supply-chain risk. It builds on existing operational resilience requirements and does not introduce new regulatory obligations. The consultation closes on February 26.

The regulators also issued supplementary guidance on cyber risks related to frontier AI and future quantum computing. Katharine Braddick, chief executive of the Prudential Regulation Authority and a deputy governor of the Bank of England, said cyberattacks were becoming more frequent, sophisticated and disruptive. She said regulators need to be confident that firms have robust cybersecurity controls and can quickly detect, contain and recover from incidents.

data.title: MetaComp Raises Nearly $10 Million from Tether and Further in Pre-A+ Extension
data.description: Singapore-based payments company MetaComp said it received nearly $10 million in additional strategic investment for its Pre-A+ round from Tether and Further Asset Management. According to PANews, citing PR Newswire, the investment brings MetaComp’s total Pre-A financing to about $45 million, with proceeds allocated to regulatory capabilities, compliance infrastructure and payment channels in key markets. MetaComp operates a hybrid stablecoin and fiat payments business, and says its infrastructure reduces settlement times along the Asia-Middle East-Africa corridor from two to seven days to less than 24 hours. The expansion follows $35 million in Pre-A and Pre-A+ funding completed in March 2026.

data.title: CoinShares CEO Blames AI for Bitcoin’s Slide as AI Stocks Also Fall
data.description: CoinShares CEO Jean-Marie Mognetti blamed AI for draining capital from crypto as Bitcoin fell about 24% in a month, while AI stocks also declined. He said AI was absorbing marginal dollars that might otherwise have gone to digital assets, according to BeInCrypto. Nvidia fell 2.9% on Wednesday despite beating earnings estimates, and the S&P 500 lost 0.23%, its fifth straight decline; the Nasdaq Composite rose 0.42%. A basket of 62 chip stocks lost more than $650 billion over two sessions last week. Great Valley Advisor Group chief market strategist Eric Parnell said the sector remained fragile amid AI spending and debt financing. Anthropic’s IPO is set for this week, with shares expected to price above the $70-to-$78 range, CNBC reported. Mognetti said a strong debut could lift risk assets, while a weak one could raise doubts about AI financing and revive crypto’s debasement narrative. Bitcoin traded near $62,300 on Thursday, down 23% since Sept. 30, compared with a 19% decline before SpaceX’s June listing.

data.title: Anthropic Prices IPO at $83 per Share, Valuing SK Telecom Stake at $3.2 Billion
data.description:
According to ChainCatcher citing Chosun Biz, Anthropic priced its IPO at $83 per share, above the previously marketed range, valuing SK Telecom’s stake at about $3.2 billion. Following a 10-for-1 stock split in September, the stake represents approximately 38.6 million shares. Anthropic and its seven co-founders are raising a record $107.3 billion through the expanded IPO and private placements.

SK Telecom has invested about 272 billion won, or $204 million, since 2023. At the IPO price, its holding is worth roughly 15.7 times its cumulative investment, with paper gains approaching 10 times the company’s 2025 net income attributable to shareholders. SK Telecom disclosed in June that it held 3.86 million shares and declined to comment on its current position. Its shares fell about 6% in early trading Thursday; through Wednesday’s close, they had gained 50% in 2026.

SK Hynix and Samsung Electronics participated in Anthropic’s $65 billion financing in May, when the company was valued at $965 billion. Chosun Biz reported that each invested billions of dollars, though neither disclosed its stake. SK Hynix said it joined Series H to build relationships with potential customers and declined to disclose the amount; Samsung declined to comment. A filing also showed that TSMC, Micron, and Nvidia agreed to participate in a $26 billion private placement alongside the IPO.

data.title: STOCKS | New World Development Shares Fall 54%, Face Worst Week on Rights Issue
data.description: According to Bloomberg, New World Development Co. shares have fallen 54% and are on track for their worst week on record as a heavily discounted rights issue shakes investor confidence. Analysts have downgraded the indebted Hong Kong developer.
